title: 911 service down across Ontario and parts of Canada
summary: Access to 911 service is down across parts of Canada and Ontario, including in Toronto, Waterloo and Winnipeg, according to emergency response services.

image.caption: 911 service is down across many parts of Ontario and in some cities across Canada on Thursday morning. (Michael Wilson/CBC)

blocks.text: Access to 911 service is down across parts of Canada and Ontario, including in Toronto, Waterloo and Winnipeg, according to emergency response services.
Anyone in need of 911 urged to contact non-emergency lines
Residents in need of emergency services and unable to contact 911 are being urged to contact any available non-emergency lines.

All emergency services in Toronto, Durham Region and Ontario Provincial Police services across the provinces shared on social media platform X that they are still experiencing an outage of their 911 services as of 5:40 a.m. Thursday.
But police in York and Peel region in the Greater Toronto Area, shared on X that their service is now back up and running.
Bell 911 service is down across Ontario, a spokesperson with Toronto paramedics told CBC News.
They said typically 911 calls are filtered and transferred by dispatchers with the Toronto police.
How to reach Toronto emergency services
Toronto paramedics said anyone needing their assistance Thursday morning should still call 911, as some calls have still been coming through this morning.
Toronto police shared on X that anyone needing emergency assistance should reach out to their non-emergency line at 416-808-2222 or directly contact their local division.
Toronto Fire said on X they can be contacted through their non-emergency line at 416-338-9000.
